items.title: Source-reported precursors, solvent and graphite substrate
paragraphs: Cu(CH3COO)2 (hydrate unspecified) and thiourea were dissolved sequentially in DEG. Their stated concentrations are 20 mM and 10 mM. Total solution volume, batch scale and which solute was added first are not specified.
Flexible graphite paper was annealed in air at 450 °C for 30 min. Teflon autoclave is apparatus, not a reagent.

items.title: Impedance measurement and author interpretation
paragraphs: Impedance spectra were collected under illumination at Voc using a 10 mV AC perturbation from 0.1 to 100000 Hz with a Zahner IM6ex and fit using Z-view. The authors assign the high-frequency semicircle to counter-electrode/electrolyte charge-transfer resistance and report 0.063 Ω cm² for Nano-Cu2S/C. J0 = 205 mA cm−2 is their Rct-derived value using n = 2, not a direct measurement; the exact device/batch assignment is not reported.

items.title: Chemical intuition and interpretation
paragraphs: The authors motivate a low-cost flexible counter-electrode alternative and use a conductive graphite sheet as the deposition substrate. They suggest air annealing creates surface functionality that can aid particle adhesion, and interpret dispersed Cu2S as providing useful reaction area; these explanations are author interpretation, not separately measured causal mechanisms.
